questions.question: Day 10 Practice (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)): When talking about rescheduling a team sync (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'I'?

options.a: Shift meeting 3 clock possible? yesterday
options.b: Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?
options.c: I am rescheduling a team sync right now.
options.d: Shift meeting 3 clock possible?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?".

questions.question: Day 10 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'pick out'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: Carefully choose specific items from a group.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question: Day 10 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'follow up'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: Check progress on a prior matter.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'follow up' means: check progress on a prior matter. Example: "I will follow up with the team regarding the report."

questions.question: Day 10 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'freshen up'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: Wash hands and face to relax after travel.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
'freshen up' means: wash hands and face to relax after travel. Example: "Let me freshen up after returning home."

questions.question: Day 10 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'call off'?

options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

Correct: Option A
'call off' means: cancel a planned event or meeting. Example: "They had to call off the afternoon presentation."

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 1 (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ ఒప్పందంలో కొన్ని మార్పులు చేస్తే బాగుంటుంది."
(Literal attempt: "In agreement some changes if do good.")

options.a: It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement.
options.b: I am needing to in agreement some changes if do good.
options.c: In agreement some changes if do good.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement."

Use executive diplomacy 'It would be advantageous to...'.

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 2 (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.
options.c: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.d: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 3 (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "మీ ఆలోచన బాగుంది కానీ మన బడ్జెట్ దానికి అనుమతించదు."
(Literal attempt: "Your thought good but budget not allow.")

options.a: Your thought good but budget not allow.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to your thought good but budget not allow.
options.d: While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it."

Use diplomatic contrast 'While your proposal is insightful...'.

questions.question:
Day 10 Translation Scenario 4 (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.b: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.c: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.
